title: Parse a pasted list of email addresses
prompt:
For the invite dialog, add src/emails.js exporting parseEmailList(text) that returns { valid: string[], invalid: string[] }.

Splitting: the text is split on any run of commas, semicolons and whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines); empty pieces are ignored. Each piece is checked as-is, no other trimming or unwrapping (so "<ada@example.com>" is just invalid).

An address is valid when:
- it contains exactly one "@";
- the local part (before "@") is 1-64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ % + -, does not start or end with ".", and has no "..";
- the domain is two or more labels separated by "."; each label is 1-63 letters, digits or hyphens and does not start or end with a hyphen; the last label is letters only and at least 2 long.

valid lists valid addresses in input order, spelled as typed, without duplicates: addresses that differ only in letter case are the same, and the first spelling is the one kept. invalid lists every invalid piece in input order, including repeats.
acceptance: Splitting on runs of commas/semicolons/whitespace, empty input, allowed local-part characters, invalid pieces in order with repeats, local-part dot rules and 64-char limit, domain label rules (hyphens, characters, empty labels, TLD letters only and >= 2, 63-char labels), case-insensitive de-duplication keeping first spelling, display names treated as invalid pieces.
difficulty_rationale: One function with explicit validation rules and a de-duplication rule.
